audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Warwick six of seven rows including two-plus items, while the why-text under those same rows said 'level 2 is even', 'levels 4-5 are skill-based', 'first item is even' and 'two-plus items favours Nasus'.
audit.why: The content whys were written against the packet chart [Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Skill, Nasus]; the side values were never updated. 49.11% win rate matches an even lane that decays late.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 3, 5 set to Skill, row 4 to Warwick, row 6 to Nasus, on both layers as matched pairs, with ratings and phases[N].why rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blood Hunt was described as a general trade-winner and the first-item row as a Warwick spike.
audit.why: Blood Hunt only grants speed and attack speed against enemies already under 50% health, tripling under 25% — it finishes fights, it does not start them. Nasus' spike is permanent Siphoning Strike stacks, which nothing you buy resets.
audit.corrected: Spike text now keys the early window to Jaws of the Beast's 8s lunge and Primal Howl, and calls the first item even.

audit.whatIsWrong: Warwick was credited with a 'Q reset' and Spirit Fire with shredding 'your resistances'.
audit.why: The auto reset in this matchup is Nasus' Siphoning Strike, not Warwick's Q — Jaws of the Beast is a 365-range lunge that heals for damage dealt. Spirit Fire reduces armour only, on a flat 12s cooldown. Wither (15/14/13/12/11s) cuts move AND attack speed, which is what actually kills your chase.
audit.corrected: Removed the false Q reset, named Siphoning Strike, corrected Spirit Fire to armour, and attached Wither's real cooldown to the sequencing advice the packet flagged as missing.

edits.before: W attack speed turns on against low-HP targets. Only take the trade when Nasus's Wither is down.
edits.after: Blood Hunt only turns on once he is under 50% health, so level 2 is even — deny cannon stacks rather than force.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Wither's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Skill window: Wither runs 15-11s and outlasts your chase, so trade only once it is spent and deny his stacks the rest of the time.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Nasus's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress suppresses for 1.5s and Wither cannot shake it off once it lands. Fury of the Sands hands him health and resists, so open before he presses it.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Wither's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King answers his health, but Siphoning Strike stacks are permanent — first item is even.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Nasus carry threat 10/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on, his stacks have outgrown you. Nasus carry threat 10/10 — end it on the map before he ever gets a clean duel.

edits.before: Level 3 is yours: Q reset plus Blood Hunt speed lets you win any trade before his stacks matter.
edits.after: Level 3 is yours: Jaws' max-health bite and Primal Howl win trades before stacks matter.

edits.before: With Q and W online you win every extended trade before Nasus has stacks; Blood Hunt tracks him when he backs off and Jaws of the Beast heals you through his slow-fed autos.
edits.after: With Jaws of the Beast (8s) and Primal Howl online you win extended trades before Nasus has stacks; Blood Hunt only marks him under 50% health, so it finishes fights, never starts them.

edits.before: Once Nasus has hundreds of Q stacks and Spirit Fire, his on-hit shred plus Wither turns your all-in into a death sentence; do not solo him past two items.
edits.after: Once Nasus has hundreds of Siphoning Strike stacks, Spirit Fire cuts your armour and an 11s Wither ends your chase; do not solo him past two items.

edits.before: From level 3 to 6 you dominate — your Q reset and W movement speed win every skirmish, and at 6 Infinite Duress ignores his Wither to burst him; punish hard here because it only gets worse.
edits.after: From level 3 to 6 you press — Jaws' max-health bite and Primal Howl win skirmishes, and at 6 Infinite Duress suppresses him straight through Wither; punish hard, because it only gets worse.

edits.before: Trading into his full burst window with E down — fear is your trade-flipper; without it you are just a sustain bot.

notes: Packet flagged zero cooldown-sequencing cues; the rewrites now carry Wither 15-11s, Spirit Fire flat 12s and Jaws 8s. Whether Infinite Duress' suppression blocks Wither's cast is standard suppression behaviour and not in Riot's text; I wrote only that Wither cannot shake the suppression once it lands, which the kit text does support.
